label: Diagram 2.1
caption: Diagram 2.1 Maximum length of ramp at a given gradient
description:
This diagram is a chart titled "Diagram 2.1 Maximum length of ramp at a given gradient". It features a graph where the vertical axis represents the "Gradient of ramp" ranging from "1:10" (steeper) to "1:20" (shallower), and the horizontal axis represents the "Maximum length of ramp flight (m)" ranging from 0 to 10. The vertical axis also labels "Rise (mm)" reaching up to "500".

A black line plotted on the graph connects various data points. Specific points are labeled with both the length in metres on the horizontal axis and the corresponding rise in millimetres. For example, at a length of 1m, the rise is "83"; at 2m, it is "166"; at 4m, it is "286"; at 5m, it is "333"; at 6m, it is "375"; at 7m, it is "412"; at 8m, it is "444"; at 9m, it is "474"; and at 10m, the rise is "500".

The area below and to the right of the line is shaded grey, labeled as "does not comply", while the area above the line is white, labeled as "satisfactory". Two notes are provided: "1. Gradient x length of flight = rise e.g. 1/20 x 10 = 500mm." and "2. A site gradient of 1:15 will usually require a series of ramps of 1:12 interspersed with landings where necessary."
